CONTENT-1.note: Verified: multer 2.0.2 (now 2.4.0 after npm audit fix) no longer crashes on a truncated multipart body. Additionally server/index.ts no longer shuts the process down on a single uncaughtException (logs it; only 10 within a minute end the process so the supervisor restarts it).

AUTH-1.note: shared/schema.ts: updateProfileSchema is an explicit z.object reusing usernameField/emailField of insertUserSchema (trim, 3-30, charset, email, max 254); handler compares with !== undefined, so '' is validated and rejected.

AUTH-3.note: server/index.ts: cors() delegate allows credentials only for the request's own origin and CORS_ORIGINS (server/utils/origins.ts, documented in .env.example, passed through docker-compose.yml); 'null' and any other origin get no ACAO.

AUTH-4.note: Auth routes are registered by registerAuthRoutes() after app.use('/api', validateCsrf) (server/routes/index.ts), so login/register/logout need the CSRF token; express.urlencoded removed (no cross-site form posts).

AUTH-5.note: Ordering fix: setupSession() (session+passport) -> banCheckMiddleware -> maintenance -> CSRF -> registerAuthRoutes(). Frozen accounts get 403 on PATCH /api/profile(/password); POST /api/logout stays allowed for frozen/banned clients.

AUTH-7.note: Sessions store authStamp = sha256(password hash) at login/register; deserializeUser rejects sessions whose stamp differs (and stamp-less pre-fix sessions: one-time re-login after deploy). Password change regenerates the current session (new id, stamp, same CSRF token flow) and closes the user's WebSockets; the WS upgrade checks the stamp too.

AUTH-8.note: PATCH /api/profile and /api/profile/password wrapped in try/catch -> sendInternalError; empty update -> 400 'No valid fields provided for update' (code NO_FIELDS); unique violations (23505 / SQLite UNIQUE) -> 400 'Username already taken' / 'Email already registered'.

AUTH-10.note: Profile limits: displayName 100, bio 500, location 100, website 200, image URLs 500; NUL bytes rejected; website must be http(s) with a dotted host (bare domain gets https://), javascript:/data:/vbscript: rejected. Client (lib/input-limits.ts) is stricter for displayName (50)/bio (160), which is fine.

AUTH-11.note: Unknown username runs a bcrypt compare against a dummy hash (burnPasswordCheck in server/utils/password-hash.ts).

AUTH-12.note: cookie.secure = REQUIRE_HTTPS==='true' ? true : 'auto' (req.secure honours X-Forwarded-Proto from trusted proxies); plain HTTP on localhost still gets a non-Secure cookie (regression test in core.fix).

AUTH-14.note: Per-account login lock that does not depend on the IP (20 failures / 15 min per normalized username -> 429 even for the right password; reset on success). Accepted parts: registration still names a taken username/email (e2e suite documents this as intended UX; usernames are public anyway) and there is no self-service account deletion (feature, not a fix).

UI-12.note: Server validates website as http(s) URL (see AUTH-10) with message 'Website must be an http(s) URL'; client form already validates (client agent).

UI-15.note: Client change: no password-change form exists in the client. Server endpoint PATCH /api/profile/password is ready (400 'Current password is incorrect', zod issues for newPassword incl. 'This password is too common...', 429 after 5 wrong attempts). Needs the client agent.

UI-17.note: Server: a unique-constraint race on POST /api/register now answers 400 'Username already exists'/'Email already registered' instead of 500. Client side (disable submit while form.formState.isSubmitting) is for the client agent.

ADMIN-5.note: ban-check.ts: device id is a random 128-bit id in an HttpOnly cookie 'ov_device' (issued on API requests), no longer OS+browser+language. Hardware bans match that id only. Old header-fingerprint bans stop matching (they were over-broad). Note: admins need to see device ids to ban them - activity-logger could record req.deviceFingerprint (not my file).

ADMIN-8.note: Login/deserializeUser/WS upgrade decide bans via isAccountBanned(): an active, non-expired account ban in the bans table (activeBanCondition from bulk-action-service). Karma is no longer a ban signal; bootstrapAccounts() resets the legacy -9999 ban marker to 0 once (idempotent). Regression test (needs E2E_DATABASE_URL to move expires_at into the past) passes.

ADMIN-15.note: Enforced: registration_enabled (403 REGISTRATION_DISABLED), admin_ip_allowlist (403 on /api/admin/* from other req.ip), session_timeout_minutes (idle timeout, min 5, 0=off), default_user_karma (start karma, only >0). Accepted (descriptions in settings.ts seed say so): max_login_attempts (fixed 20/15 min lock; a low configurable value lets anyone lock users out), max_usernames_per_ip (needs a stored registration IP; per-IP 5/h limiter exists), require_email_verification (no verification endpoint exists; enforcing would lock users out), max_upload_size_mb (upload limits live in the upload routes of other agents). CSV formula neutralisation is in admin code (admin agent).

INPUT-12.note: Done for my routes: register (username 30, email 254, password 128) and PATCH /api/profile (see AUTH-10), password change (current 1024, new 128). Posts, messages, reports, tickets, themes, communities, AI, admin groups are the other agents' routes.

INPUT-2.note: Karma is reputation only: login and deserializeUser no longer treat karma < 0 as banned, only an active account ban in the bans table. The e2e test 'an account with negative karma (banned) cannot log in' asserted the old rule; it now bans via POST /api/admin/bans, plus a new test 'negative karma alone is not a ban'.

SOCIAL-2.note: Verified: Origin parsing guarded; the upgrade handler is fully try/caught; origin check now via isAllowedOrigin.

SOCIAL-15.note: Sockets are registered with their session id; logout closes the sockets of that session (code 4001).

SOCIAL-16.note: services/websocket.ts: connections is Map<userId, UserSockets> (one entry per tab); close removes only that socket. UserSockets answers readyState/send like a socket, so community-access.ts works unchanged (it could use sendToUser).

SOCIAL-27.note: WS origin must be the request's own host or CORS_ORIGINS; the localhost-any-port exception is gone.

ATK-AUTH-1.note: Per-account lock (see AUTH-14) independent of X-Forwarded-For. Also TRUST_PROXY=true now trusts only loopback/private/link-local proxies, so a client hitting port 5000 directly from a public address cannot choose its IP; auth.ts no longer forces trust proxy 1 in production.

ATK-AUTH-2.note: Password change: fixed (5 wrong current passwords per account/hour -> 429, plus the per-IP limit). Registration: the attack test still fails by design of the test setup - it rotates X-Forwarded-For from 127.0.0.1, a trusted-proxy position the server cannot tell apart from real proxied traffic. In production the trust-proxy fix (only private/loopback proxies) stops spoofing from internet clients. An IP-independent global registration cap cannot be set without breaking legitimate bursts: the e2e suites register up to 33 accounts in 10 s, the attack test 15 in ~5 s.

ATK-AUTH-5.note: See AUTH-5 (ban check now runs before register/login).

ATK-AUTH-7.note: See AUTH-7 (also covers a cloned cookie of the current session: its id is regenerated).

ATK-AUTH-8.note: server/utils/password-hash.ts: new hashes are '$sha256-bcrypt$' + bcrypt(base64(sha256(password))); legacy $2b$ and scrypt hashes still verify and are re-hashed on login (legacy bcrypt only when the password is <= 72 bytes). db-migrations.ts uses the same helpers.

ATK-AUTH-10.note: Maintenance middleware now runs before the auth routes: register 503 (MAINTENANCE_REGISTRATION), profile/password edits 503 for non-staff; login/logout/user/csrf-token stay reachable.

ATK-AUTH-15.note: shared/common-passwords.ts blocklist (~100 most common 8+ char passwords, case-insensitive) in insertUserSchema.password and updatePasswordSchema.newPassword.

ATK-AUTH-16.note: Info trade-off: e2e/auth-account documents the explicit 'Username already exists'/'Email already registered' answers as intended (tests assert them), and usernames are enumerable through public profiles anyway. The two attack enumeration tests stay red by decision.

ATK-AUTH-17.note: Registration and profile renames refuse INITIAL_OWNER_USERNAME (case-insensitive) while it is not taken; seedInitialOwner logs CRITICAL when an account with that name exists, has another password and is not owner (possible squatter).

ATK-XSS-4.note: One helmet configuration in server/index.ts for every response (script-src 'self' outside development, frame-ancestors 'none'); the second helmet in routes/index.ts is removed; /uploads keeps a stricter own CSP (default-src 'none', sandbox).

ATK-RT-1.note: ws.on('error') per connection (terminate the socket), wss.on('error'), socket error handler on upgrade; uncaughtException no longer shuts down (see CONTENT-1). Crash test passes.

ATK-RT-3.note: WebSocketServer maxPayload 64 KiB; an oversized frame closes only that socket (regression test).

ATK-RT-4.note: A missing Origin is still accepted: browsers always send Origin on WS handshakes, so a request without it cannot be cross-site; it still needs a valid session (now also stamp + ban checked). The realtime suite asserts this behaviour.

ATK-RT-5.note: Upgrades to any path other than /ws get 404 and the socket is destroyed (in development Vite HMR upgrades are left to Vite).

ATK-RT-6.note: npm audit fix (no --force): critical 2 -> 0, high 17 -> 6, total 24 -> 11 for --omit=dev (ws 8.22.0, multer 2.4.0, compression 1.8.2, proxy-addr 2.0.8, express-rate-limit 8.7.1, axios 1.20.0, tar 7.5.22, ...). Unit tests 25/25 and npm run build pass. Accepted remaining: sharp 0.34.5 (fix is 0.35.x, semver-major: needs testing of the image pipeline), i18next-http-backend (fix 4.x major; client-side, loads only our own /locales paths), qs 6.14.2 (pinned by express 4.22.1; no fix in that range), tailwindcss/tailwindcss-animate/chokidar/braces/micromatch/fast-glob/postcss-selector-parser/postcss-nested (build-time CSS tooling, not executed by the server at runtime; should move to devDependencies).

ATK-RT-7.note: connect-src 'self' ws://<host> wss://<host> (host validated) instead of bare ws:/wss:.
